asks.asks: LIN-4504's live cutover cannot start: the fleet pause is refused. The pause is the first step of the cutover, and nothing may be captured or applied until it is set. Refusal quoted from POST /api/proxy/dispatch/halt with {"mode":"pause"}: 409 PROXY_TOKEN_UNBOUND, "This token is not bound to a workspace, so it cannot halt the runner. Mint a new token on the Proxy page, or use the Dispatch page." GET /api/proxy/dispatch/halt reads {"halt":null}, so nothing is paused. Which way do you want the pause set?

asks.asks: Ruling 1 (slice 3, piece P8 / LIN-4521): when close-out pushes its own fix commit after the approval, the approval becomes stale. Should merging then wait for a quick re-review of the new head? Records can show the approval as stale but can't stop the merge: close-out merges inside its own session (--match-head-commit), and Harbour's recorders run afterwards. So a yes is enforced by a close-out prompt rule: after its own push, close-out writes a finding to review naming the new head and parks instead of merging, and P5's live-wait fix lets the re-review run beside it. It costs about one run per task.
asks.short: Should merging then wait for a quick re-review of the new head?

asks.asks: Ruling 2 (slice 3, piece P4 / LIN-4517): open tasks that were reviewed by comment have no verdict record at cutover. Should those verdicts be imported once (a one-off script, never committed, that pins each to the head findSha guesses, runs before the flip, and is discarded before findSha is retired), or should each such task be re-reviewed as it comes up? This also decides how far back the measures can read: with no import, they start at the cutover instant, and P1's committed readings cover the history before it.
asks.short: Should those verdicts be imported once, or should each such task be re-reviewed as it comes up?

asks.asks:
LIN-4416 shortlist, as you asked: approve before anything is built? The re-plan (plan-33a70884 v2) picks two themes, about five issues, each one rule in one place, both in LinearViewer only:

1. Verdict authority (LIN-3386 verdict half, LIN-3402 item 2, plus finding-a75343af and finding-071b3def). Any run can write a review Approve today and the merge/Done gate accepts it, which makes every other limit advisory. Fix: only the judging stage may write a verdict, a withdrawn verdict stops counting, and a dispatch holder can't start a review run with its own prompt.
2. One report gate on every lane (LIN-2576). The periodical report gate runs on only one of the routes that can set Done, and it has topped a Periodical's findings five times. Fix: one shared gate called by all of them.

Left in the backlog: who may end a close-out finding (finding-5dcf7993, the next candidate, which needs its own production count first); the merge credential (LIN-3417, which needs a separate worker identity, your call); member-minted tokens (LIN-4215, your call); tokens in prompt text and untrusted tracker text (LIN-3387); and the rest of the 134 as they are.

Yes = build these two as written (breakdown into two child tasks, then plan review, build, review, close-out). No = name what to add or swap, and the plan is redone to that before anything is built.
asks.short: LIN-4416 shortlist, as you asked: approve before anything is built?

asks.asks:
LIN-4416: the plan for your three verdict rules has been sent back three times, and Harbour stopped the plan/review cycle for you to decide whether it goes on. One more plan round, or stop here?

What happened: rules 1 (only the judging stage writes a verdict) and 2 (withdrawn verdicts stop counting) have passed review every time. Rule 3 (a caller can't start a judging run with its own prompt) has not: each review found another way round it, first by adding a followUpTo, then by leaving `kind` out and sending promptName 'Review', which the server turns into a review run (finding-6cf58138, checked in code). The pattern is that rule 3 checked the shape of the request instead of the kind the run will actually get.

The fix is that root, not another special case: rule 3 tests the kind the dispatch will really get, through one shared helper the dispatch code already uses, so no request shape gets round it. The blocked step checked this and found nothing outside the task in the way.

Yes = one more plan round (v5) with that fix, then plan review, build, review and close-out. Stop = nothing is built; the plan stays at v4 and the hole stays open.
asks.short: One more plan round, or stop here?

asks.asks:
LIN-4416, PR #2514 is built with CI green, and review found one more way round rule 3. Ship what's done, or one more build round?

Where it stands (review verdict-e4c62314, request-changes): rule 1 (only the judging stage writes a verdict) and rule 2 (a withdrawn verdict stops counting) are met. CI is green on e94465efd, and the full suite passes merged onto current main (25,150 tests, 0 failures). Rule 3 is met on POST /dispatch, but not on recommend-and-dispatch: send a custom dispatch with your own instructions, then recommend-and-dispatch {kind:'review', followUpTo:<that row>}, and a review run (writing as review) starts inside the session you filled (finding-a1ed48c1, probed). Nothing legitimate uses that route today.

The pattern: this is the fifth way round rule 3 (plan rounds found followUpTo and promptName, now this). Each time the check sat on one route's request rather than on the row that actually starts a run. The fix the reviewer gives is small (a judging run must start in a fresh session: refuse a judging kind with followUpTo on the recommend lane), but it is again one route.

Cost of waiting: nothing is merged, so until this lands any run can still write an Approve the merge/Done gate accepts (the hole rules 1 and 2 close).
asks.short: Ship what's done, or one more build round?

LIN-4549 (piece 1/7 of LIN-4546), PR #2516: CI is green on head 14ea474 and review has approved twice, but the merge keeps slipping by one review round. Do we pin review a third time, or change the rule that causes the loop?

Where it stands: review approved 84944f5d, then 5b5e444, then af37497, each time with one small condition. The latest delta is one five-line comment in lib/chat-tools.js that review itself wrote out word for word. Nothing is merged; pieces 2 to 7 of LIN-4546 are held behind this one.

Cost of waiting: nothing lands and LIN-4546 stays open; no harm is done meanwhile.
